source.title: Practical Unlearning for Large Language Models
source.authors: Chongyang Gao; Lixu Wang; Kai-Ze Ding; Chenkai Weng; Xiao Wang; Qi Zhu

record.file_problem: The supplied title differs from the paper title in the text (“On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning”); the text is otherwise present in full.
record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery after unlearning using a targeted relearning attack, a different method aimed at the same recovery question.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the targeted relearning results in Appendix F.9, comparing unlearned models before and after fine-tuning on OpenbookQA validation data. The main unlearning benchmark results and OOD-detector AUROC results are not recovery-attack outcomes.
record.test_reason: Appendix F.9 applies a targeted relearning attack (Hu et al. 2024, public-information setting) to PO, SOPO and the authors' O3 after ScienceQA unlearning. It reports targeted accuracy before and after the attack, which bears on B, on A for the baseline methods, and on F for O3. Appendix G.2 also tests O3 against character-level adversarial perturbation of inputs.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors state O3 is significantly more robust to targeted relearning, with a D.U. change of 3.7 versus 24 (PO) and 30.3 (SOPO), and the best post-attack performance. They do not discuss O3's post-attack utility loss.
record.recipe_differences: O3 uses an orthogonally regularized LoRA with an OOD detector and soft-weighted inference; this is not a reproduction of the original unlearning methods. The tested attack is targeted fine-tuning on related OpenbookQA validation examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The recovery outcome differs by unlearning method: O3 shows smaller changes than PO and SOPO under the same reported targeted relearning setup.
record.problems: The targeted relearning evidence covers one model and one related-data attack setting; the number of attack examples is not stated in the reported result, and Table 19 gives no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional targeted-relearning result rows are reported in Appendix F.9. Other unlearning benchmarks and OOD-detection ablations were left out because they do not measure recovery from the targeted relearning attack.

untested.parts: Near-chance accuracy of the original methods (RMU/WHP) and their resistance to quantization, prompting or internal edits.
Unrelated relearning data; a subset of the forgotten facts; different relearning set sizes (size not stated); models other than LLaMA2-7b; datasets other than ScienceQA.

No activation ablation or deletion-versus-blocking analysis. Appendix B openly describes O3 as an external blocking design (base weights frozen, LoRA gated by an OOD detector), but this is a design statement, not a test.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attack on the baselines. Only a character-perturbation attack on O3's detector (G.2).

O3 is not tested against quantization, activation edits, jailbreaks or multilingual prompting. It is also not tested against relearning on the forgotten facts themselves, or against an attacker who removes the gating.

missing.what: Utility columns (R.D., CommonsenseQA, OpenbookQA) before and after relearning for PO, SOPO and O3. O3's OpenbookQA utility drops 80.8 to 72.6 after the attack.
Adversarial character-perturbation attack on O3's unlearning-knowledge detector on TOFU: S.U./D.U. barely change (e.g. request 3 D.U. 19.5 vs 19.7) and AUROC stays above 92.
Number of relearning examples and relearning hyperparameters are not stated, and it is unclear which parameters the attack fine-tunes (base weights or the gated LoRA).

record.verdict_notes: O3 keeps the base LLM frozen and applies an unlearning LoRA only when an OOD detector flags the input. By the authors' own account (Appendix B) it blocks access rather than deleting knowledge, which is conceptually relevant to C but untested. With random-label unlearning on multiple-choice QA, accuracies below chance (e.g. 9.3) mean small rises may not indicate recovered knowledge. Only one model (LLaMA2-7b), one relearning setting, and no uncertainty in Table 19. The record's title mismatch is noted; the paper is 'On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning' (ICLR 2025).

versions.untested_parts: The study reports unlearning performance and utility, but does not establish that targeted accuracy is near chance or test the full claim that simple attacks do not recover it.
Tests one targeted relearning set of science-related OpenbookQA validation questions; does not test unrelated examples or a subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion is tested.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context-information attack is tested.
Tests O3 against the targeted relearning attack only, not resistance to internal edits, quantization, or prompting attacks.

relation.reason: Reports targeted accuracy before and after relearning, which bears on B, A and F.

tranche.reason: A different method (O3), plus the Hu et al. targeted relearning attack applied to PO, SOPO and O3. Same question; not a reproduction.

source_check.notes: Table 19 has no uncertainty (the paper says three seeds) and no relearning epochs or steps. O3 S.U. 9.3 is below multiple-choice chance (random-label unlearning), so part of its rise may be a return toward chance. SOPO's 60.9 may be only partial restoration; base accuracy appears only in a figure. The text's title is the v2 title 'On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning'.

statements.problem: No error about this study. The statement cites its rows but never names it. The rows fit the claim: on LLaMA2-7b ScienceQA, OpenbookQA-validation relearning lifts PO S.U. 59.9 -> 86.2 and SOPO S.U. 29.6 -> 60.9.
None. PO and SOPO rise 24-31 points and O3 +6.2 (S.U.) under the same OpenbookQA relearning on LLaMA2-7b.
No error about this study. It cites F9-O3-DU but never names O3. Its conditions (1B-3B models, TOFU/LKF/FaithUn/WMDP-cyber) do not cover this row, though the row fits the resistance claim.

statements.correction: Pre-attack, O3 R.D./CommonQA/OpenbookQA are 91.1/78.5/80.8, against PO 90.8/75.8/77.6 and SOPO 89.7/76.8/77.8. After relearning, O3 OpenbookQA is 80.8 -> 72.6 and CommonQA 78.5 -> 75.0. SOPO OpenbookQA also falls, 77.8 -> 72.0. Drop F9-O3-SU and F9-O3-DU from this statement.
statements.problem: The statement cites O3 rows as evidence that resistance costs capability. This study shows no such cost: O3 has the best pre-attack utility, and the post-attack falls come from the attack.
